Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

In last class you have studied definition, properties and graph of gamma function.

Key details

  • In this class, we are going to study definition of beta function and properties of beta function.
  • Beta function is a definite integral whose integrant depends on two variables.
  • It is also known as Euler's integral of first time.
  • Beta function is defined as beta of m comma n is equal to integral 0 to 1 x power m minus 1 into 1 minus x power n minus 1 is, where m and n both are positive.
  • Let me call this as equation number one.
  • We can also have an alternate form for beta function.
  • We can get it by putting x is equal to sine square theta in equation number 1.
  • When x is equal to sine square theta, dx is equal to two sine theta cos theta d theta.
  • Also, the limits of integration change with the substitution.
  • When x is equal to 0, that implies sine square theta is equal to 0, that implies theta is equal to 0.
  • When x is equal to 1, that means sine square theta is equal to 1, or theta is equal to pi by 2.
  • With this, we will get beta of m comma n as integral 0 to pi by 2, sin square theta all power m minus 1.
  • One minus sine square theta whole power n minus one into two sine theta cos theta b theta.
  • 2 is a constant we can keep outside the integral sign.
  • Sin square theta wall power m minus 1 is sin power 2 m minus 2 theta.
  • One minus sin square theta we know it is cos square theta.
  • Beta of m comma n is now two times integral 0 to pi by 2 sin power 2 m minus 1 theta cos power 2n minus 1 theta d theta.
  • This is another form of beta function, we can also call it as trigonometric form of beta function.
  • Both the forms are important, so you can remember both the forms here.
  • Both are useful when solving the problems.
  • We can choose any one of these forms according to our convenience.
  • Next, we will study the properties of beta function.
  • First property is symmetry, which states beta of m comma n is equal to beta of L comma n.
  • We can prove this by using the definition of beta function, which states beta of m, n is equal to integral 0 to 1 x power m minus 1 into 1 minus x power n minus 1 dx.
  • then dx becomes minus of dt.
  • Also the limits of integration change with the substitution x equal to 1 minus t implies t is equal to 1 minus x.
  • Therefore, when x is equal to 0, t is equal to 1.
  • And when x is equal to 1, right, t is equal to 0.
  • Therefore, now we can have beta of m comma n is equal to integral 1 to 0 1 minus t power m minus 1 t power n minus 1 minus t.
  • T power n minus 1 minus t to the power m minus 2 t, which is nothing but equal to beta of n comma m.
  • Thus we have proved now beta of m comma n is exactly same as beta of n comma m.
  • And now we know beta of m n is same as beta of n m, so we can also write beta of m, comma n is equal to 2 times integral 0 to pi by 2 cos power 2 m minus 1 theta into sine power 2n minus 1 theta d.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

To prove this, consider the diagnometric form of beta function that is beta of m, comma n is equal to 2 times integral 0 to pi by 2 sin power 2m minus 1 theta cos power 2n minus 1 theta d theta.

Key details

  • Take 2m minus 1 is equal to p and 2n minus 1 is equal to q.
  • Then we get m is equal to p plus 1 by 2 and n is equal to q plus 1 divided by 2.
  • According to the definition of beta function, we should have m in beta of m comma n, m and n both are positive.
  • So, m is greater than 0 implies now p plus 1 divided by 2 is greater than 0, that means p is greater than minus 1.
  • This is what the conditions mentioned in property number 2.
  • Therefore, integral 0 to pi by 2 sine power p theta cos power q theta d theta is equal to 1 by 2 times beta of p plus 1 by 2, comma q plus 1 divided by 2.
  • This is also an important property.
  • Whenever we come across the integrals in the form integral 0 to pi by 2, sin power p theta, cos power q theta, always we can express them in terms of beta functions.
  • Already we proved now that integral 0 to pi by 2 sin power p theta cos power q theta d theta is 1 by 2 times beta of p plus 1 by 2 comma q plus 1 by 2.
  • Then we get integral 0 to pi by 2 sin power p theta is e theta is equal to 1 by 2 times beta of p plus 1 by 2 comma 0 plus 1 divided by 2.
  • Which is equal to 1 by 2 times beta of P plus 1 by 2, comma 1 by 2.
  • And also we know that beta of m comma n is equal to beta of n, comma m.
  • Thus we can conclude integral 0 to pi by 2 sine power p theta d theta is same as integral 0 to pi by 2 cos power p theta d theta and that is equal to half into beta of p plus 1 by 2 comma 1 by 2.
  • Next property says that we can also express beta function in the form of an improper integral 0 to infinity x power m minus 1 divided by 1 plus x power m plus n dx.
  • This property is also very useful because whenever we want to evaluate the integrals in the form integral 0 to infinity x power m minus 1 by 1 plus x power m plus n dx, always we can write them as beta of m comma n and we can find the value of beta of m comma n easily.
